newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed, delivery near.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed, delivery near.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Thursday with investors continuing to liquidate long positions in the July 1997 contract due to deliver on July 22, traders said.
The contract, the market's most active, ended at an intraday low of 3,167 yuan ($382) per tonne, losing 75 yuan. It opened at a high of 3,250 yuan per tonne.
September fell 43 to 3,245 yuan per tonne, November six to 3,240, the January 1998 contract rose 49 to 3,169 and March 10 to 3,130 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 28,100 tonnes from 24,400 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Investors are eager to liquidate their positions in the July contract, which depressed the confidence of long position holders in other short-term contracts," one trader said.
"Later-maturing contracts rose today due to over-selling in the past few days," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to fall steadily in the short term due to a lack of buying interest.
